newsitem.title: USA: NYC new financing arm to sell debt in Aug or Sept.
newsitem.headline: NYC new financing arm to sell debt in Aug or Sept.

text.p: New York City said on Wednesday that a new financing arm, the New York City Transitional Financing Authority, which would sidestep the city's debt cap, might start bond sales as soon as August.

Joe Lhota, the city's budget director, said: "We're currently expecting to have the first issue in either August or September of 1997." He made the comments during an interview with Reuters Financial Television, which will be shown on Thursday at 1515 EST/2015 GMT.

Lhota, saying Gov George Pataki was expected to sign the bill that will create the new authority as soon as Wednesday, explained that, within the next two weeks, he will be meeting with the city comptroller to iron out the details, including how the underwriters will be selected. The process of getting the bonds rated was anticipated to take three to four months.
A spokesman for Pataki reiterated that the governor expects to sign the bill as soon as it has been reviewed by counsel. He had no further information immediately available.

New York City needs another financing arm because its debt cap is based on a five-year average of real estate prices and fails to fully reflect the market's rebound since a local recession in the early 1990s.

In fiscal 1998, which starts on July 1, New York City likely will use the new financing arm to issue a little less than $1.3 billion of debt, with sales of general obligation bonds running around $1.3 billion.
"And that will be the total extent of our bonding program for the first year," he said.
